public_rationale: The firm part of the claim is that Cognition's business loses hundreds of millions of dollars. Press reports relaying The Information say Cognition burned about $200 million in Q2 2026 and plans to burn about $800 million in 2026, mostly on leased Nvidia servers. That fits 'hundreds of millions'. The parts about 'burning billions more' and 'a chance to make less revenue than Duolingo' are hedged views about the future, so they are not scored. For context, Duolingo made $298.5 million in revenue in Q2 2026 and was profitable. One caveat: the same report says the core business, excluding model training, is close to cash-flow neutral.
limitations: The figures are press-reported estimates from a private company, not audited results.
Cash burn is used as the measure of losses.
The only readable source relays The Information secondhand.

our_interpretation: The firm, testable part is that Cognition's business loses hundreds of millions of dollars.

The surrounding text names Cognition's burn of about $200 million in Q2 2026 and an expected burn of about $800 million for the year. So the plain reading of 'loses hundreds of millions' is a cash burn or loss of at least $200 million over a recent period. Q2 2026 is the period the post itself names.
'Necessitates burning billions more' and 'for a chance to make less revenue than Duolingo' are hedged, forward-looking judgments. They are not scored. Duolingo figures appear only as context.
Cash burn is accepted as the measure of 'loses', because the speaker's own context presents the loss as burn and no audited accounts exist for this private company.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports show Cognition burned or lost roughly $200 million or more in Q2 2026, or a similar recent period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reports show Cognition was near breakeven or lost well under $100 million in the period, so that 'hundreds of millions' overstates its losses.
